code.why: The descriptor's credentialDoor: the World's runtime calls it at boot to issue an application's TINYBIRD_API_KEY. The life and the published examples make their Workspace on the console's pages and read its tokens there, and boot no application.
Answered only in a World started read-only (the x-volter-read-only header the runtime sets), which refuses every write; the life and the published examples walk a World that writes.
The World host invokes the generated HTTP server around the pack fetch. The in-memory journey runner calls that fetch directly and starts no host listener.
Only a client that sends the Events API a line that is not JSON reaches it: Dub's zod-bird writes each event with JSON.stringify, and the Data Sources API's NDJSON is the CLI's own export.
